answer: Each epoch, the network pings every agent ID at the same random second with a walnut puzzle, a memory-hard hash that ties up 2 GB of RAM for 40 seconds. An ID that misses the deadline earns nothing that epoch. Because every ID is challenged at once, a farm can't reuse one machine across its fakes, so 200 fakes need 400 GB sitting idle. A bridge check links late answers that come from one subnet and halves rewards for every ID behind it. Cheap shared hosting stops working, and the hardware bill spirals with each added fake.
